newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK flat supply to increase till 2001 - lands chief.
newsitem.headline: HK flat supply to increase till 2001 - lands chief.

text.p: The supply of flats in Hong Kong will grow next year and increase steadily in the three years to 2001, director of lands Bob Pope said on Thursday.

"A provisional forecast for next year is about 36,000 units and we expect supply to increase steadily between 1999 and 2001," Pope told a real estate seminar organised by the American Chamber of Commerce.
"In fact, last financial year my department completed land transactions that will provide 40,000 flats."
The supply of flats in 1997 would likely remain at around the 20,000 units per year level of the past two years, he said.
Repeating figures already released by the government, Pope said 260 hectares of land would be made available for private residential development over the next five years.
"This will include 70 hectares of land for low density luxury housing where demand is highest," he said.
Some Hong Kong property developers have urged the government to increase land supply for luxury residential development, saying a larger supply is the solution to high prices.
Pope said the current surge in property prices may stem partly from the land supply figures of 1992/93 and 1993/94.
"This was not because of my department's desire to create a shortage in supply but because demand for land at that time was very low," he said.
"The good news is that flat supply figures are expected to increase from 1997 onwards in line with the increase in land supply from 1994 onwards."
Hong Kong's land administration policies would remain "business as usual" after Britain hands back the territory to China on July 1, Pope said.
